tldr: Headlines across all nine outlet groups frame Iceland's EU referendum as a live democratic event happening today. Western outlets compete on urgency language — 'tight', 'knife-edge', 'close race' — foregrounding the competitiveness of the vote rather than its substance. RT is the sole outlet whose headline reframes the vote through a NATO membership lens, implicitly staging Euro-Atlantic alignment as a sovereignty question; Nordic outlets extend the story outward to EU enlargement queue implications.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to foreground Iceland's NATO membership as the framing lens for the EU vote, implicitly casting Euro-Atlantic alignment as a sovereignty question rather than a policy choice.
Only outlet to headline the EU enlargement queue question alongside Iceland's referendum, treating the vote as a queue-setter for broader EU expansion.

bottom_line: Iceland's headline layer frames the EU referendum as a live, close-run democratic event, with 'knife-edge' urgency language dominating Western outlets and RT alone reframing it as a NATO-EU sovereignty question.
